aspect: There is no venue that works
description: Choose the West Bank and the Gaza relatives cannot come. Choose Amman and the green IDs need permits. Choose Europe and almost nobody gets a visa. The gathering cannot be held anywhere on earth.
energy_note: No country on the planet where the family can all stand.

aspect: So the funerals are the losses that compound
description: Deaths do not schedule. The relatives who cannot come do not come, and the absence is permanent in a way a missed wedding is not.
energy_note: Burying people in front of a phone screen.

aspect: Grandparents and grandchildren who have never met
description: Where the documents never align, a generation grows up knowing relatives only as voices. This is the commonest and least remarked-upon outcome of the whole regime.
energy_note: A grandmother known entirely as a phone call.

aspect: The family stops functioning as an economic unit
description: Extended families elsewhere pool childcare, housing, capital and care for the old. Fragmentation across permit regimes removes that, so each household carries alone what would have been shared.
energy_note: All the costs a family normally splits, paid singly.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the choice put to a woman at a crossing
description: Gisha documented the bind under the title 'Give up your right to live in the West Bank, or never see your children in Gaza again'. One woman was told at a crossing either to return to the West Bank as her ID address required, or to sign a form changing her address to Gaza - forcing a choice between her family home in Nablus and her son in Gaza.
energy_note: A house or a child, decided at a window.
